title: N-able says attackers accessed a Mail Assure and SpamExperts cloud server
date_note: N-able began investigating a disruption on 16 Nov; the security incident was disclosed on Wednesday 18 Nov per The Hacker News, which gives no exact disclosure date.
summary: Per The Hacker News, N-able says unknown threat actors accessed one server in its hosted Mail Assure and SpamExperts cloud, so it disabled management interfaces and APIs in the Americas, APAC and Europe. Mail flow and filtering stay available. N-able says it has no evidence customer data, including mailboxes, was compromised; its investigation continues. No attribution is given.
plain: A security vendor's email filtering service was breached. Mail still flows, but customers lost the management portal, APIs, quarantine and logs while N-able restores them.
exec: Email filtering management is offline for resellers and customers of the service; mail protection continues.
action: If you use Mail Assure or SpamExperts, follow N-able's status updates, expect no portal or API access until restored, and watch for partner notices.
impact: Management portal, APIs, quarantine and logging offline; core mail flow and filtering available; restoration under way as of 19 Nov 08:00 UTC.

validation.note: The Hacker News relays N-able's own statement; N-able's status page (uptime.n-able.com/event/202672) returned 403 to our reader, so it was not read.

review.note: Compared title, summary, impact and dates against The Hacker News (19 Nov): one server, Americas/APAC/Europe, portal/APIs/quarantine/logging offline, mail flow up, no evidence of customer data compromise, no attribution, 16 Nov start, Wednesday disclosure. Single source correctly stated; N-able stat
